How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy. There is a website called off-campus housing where you just login with your UTORid.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in Greek town and it was a great opportunity to see other neighborhoods outside downtown and experience something else that a big city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Three rounds of course enrollments. Third one was a few weeks into the semester which was great if the course wasn't what you expected. You could drop courses even further into the semester, if you'd like.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Websites, emails, previous students, Facebook groups

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted. Both on 300 and 400 level.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some courses are very popular so make sure to registrer for those in the first round. You can easily register for courses you are not sure to take cause you can easily drop them into the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 300 are way easier than 400 level courses. 400 courses remind of the level you would expect for KU. You can easily balance 4 courses, even 5 if you would like.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty much the same. Uses absalon too. PP oriented lectures and exams. No reading was required in the courses I took.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Neurogenomics HMB360
Laboratory in Neuroscience HMB310
Neuroscience: Cellular & Molecular PSL445
Neurobiology of Behaviour HMB300
Advanced Topics in Neurophysiology CSB432

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Neurogenomics HMB360 - very good teacher, teamwork, friendly environment, great syllabus
Neuroscience: Cellular & Molecular PSL445 - high tempo, higher level, new professor at every lecture
Neurobiology of Behaviour HMB300 - very interesting content, nice creative assignments
Advanced Topics in Neurophysiology CSB432 - very good teacher, you learn about the most novel research and techniques in the field, very exciting and great assignments and presentations, you learn relevant skills for a future in science and research such as presenting correctly and writing grant proposals.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds, swimming, book club, chemistry club, student parties, student bars, yoga, free fitness center

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: fitness center, swimming, the student bars

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Connect with other exchange students, hang out with your classmates from your courses, bike around in the city, visit all the great cafes

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - it is a very multicultural city and university.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are just as nervous as you. They want to connect too and make friends so just give it a try. They are very good at socializing through social media, so don't be nervous to text them and reach out.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness, openness, and the huge amount of international students.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
If you wanna learn a lot and something that is exciting to you, you have all the freedom to do so.
You will figure everything out when you get there - but it was nice to arrive 1 week or so before classes begun. 
Reach out and talk to other students. They want to make friends with you - they find exchange students especially cool hah.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Thoroughly go through the syllabus and the marking scheme.
Make a scheme over all your assignments, quizzes, attendance, exams, etc. because there is a lot and you can easily loose track and miss deadlines if not.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Get to study with other students at UofT. Making friends with people living there. Get to learn from great professors.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Keeping track of all the different courses' syllabus and deadlines. Finding out the marking scheme.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
